chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Indeed, so-and-so — a man whose name he mentioned — said: I was ascetic regarding children, until I stood at Arafat, and behold, beside me was a young boy, supplicating, weeping, and saying: O Lord! My parents! My parents! So he made me desire children when I heard that.'

key_terms.الْوَلَد: Child or children; can refer to a son specifically or offspring in general
key_terms.رَغَّبَ: To incline toward, to create desire for, to make someone wish for something
key_terms.زَاهِد: Ascetic or one who is indifferent/abstinent; here meaning one who has no desire or inclination for something worldly
key_terms.عَرَفَة: Arafat — the sacred plain near Mecca where pilgrims stand on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah during Hajj; the central rite of pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: Why did a man change his mind about having children after standing at Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a transformative moment at the sacred gathering of Arafat during Hajj, where a man who previously had no desire for children witnessed a young boy fervently supplicating for his parents. The sincerity of the boy's prayer — his tears and repeated cry of 'My parents! My parents!' — moved the narrator so deeply that his attitude toward having children completely changed. The hadith is included in the chapter on the merits of sons, illustrating that children can be a source of intercession and supplication for their parents, even while alive.
